What is Kalshi?

Kalshi has defined a new category: prediction markets. Kalshi allows people to trade on the outcome of any events and turn any question about the future into a financial asset. Kalshi fought for years and legalized prediction markets in the US for the first time in history, is currently the fastest growing financial market in America, and has thousands of markets across politics, economics, financials, weather, tech, AI, culture and more.

We believe prediction markets have the potential to be the largest financial market because they turn anything into a financial position.

  • Our vision: well… build the largest financial market on the planet.

  • Our mission: bring more truth to the world through the power of markets.

Our culture is simple: we hire really talented people, work really hard, and enjoy the climb. We are looking for ambitious and exceptional people to join our (relatively small) team to help us build the next generation of financial markets.

Role Roadmap

We are looking for someone to own institutional communications as Kalshi expands its presence with institutional investors.

You’ll develop our communications strategy, build relationships with financial and industry reporters, and drive media coverage alongside our institutional team and agency. We’re looking for a strong writer who understands exchanges, clearing, or derivatives trading and brings creative ideas, sound judgment, and the drive to own strategy through execution.

What You'll Do

  • Own Kalshi’s institutional communications strategy, identifying the audiences, outlets, and stories that matter most

  • Build relationships with reporters covering institutional markets, derivatives, exchanges, clearing, and trading

  • Proactively pitch stories that build Kalshi’s visibility and credibility with institutional audiences

  • Write press releases, media pitches, executive talking points, bylines, and other communications materials

  • Work closely with our institutional team to turn business developments and complex market topics into compelling stories

  • Partner with our agency to develop campaigns, coordinate outreach, and secure meaningful coverage

  • Use feedback from reporters and institutional audiences to sharpen our messaging and approach

What We're Looking For

  • Based in New York City

  • Mid-level communications or public relations experience in exchanges, clearing, trading, or financial market infrastructure, either in-house or at an agency

  • Strong understanding of financial markets and derivatives trading

  • Excellent writing skills and the ability to make complex financial topics clear and compelling

  • Strong financial media relationships and a track record of securing coverage

  • Creative instincts, thoughtful judgment, and the confidence to challenge conventional approaches to financial communications

  • The ability to build trust with executives, colleagues, reporters, and agency teams

  • A willingness to take responsibility and independently own work from strategy through execution

Bonus Points

  • Experience building a communications program for a new business or audience

  • Experience developing executive thought leadership and securing coverage in both institutional trade publications and broader financial media

  • Familiarity with prediction markets and their applications for institutional participants

NYC Pay Transparency Disclosure

Salary Range: $130,000 to $220,000 annually, plus equity and benefits. This range reflects current market data for this role. Kalshi has minimal hierarchy and broad variance in experience levels within each title; if your compensation expectations exceed this range, we encourage you to reach out - we’re always happy to discuss.

Our Culture

Meritocracy is at our core, and we value people who take ownership and figure (usually hard) things out. We dream big. We love our craft deeply and are proud of what we put out in the world. We are committed to our vision of building something big… but also useful: a product that brings more truth through the power of markets.

Kalshians are Kalshi’s most important asset: we pick Kalshians carefully, so we trust them fully on day 1.

Commitment to Equal Opportunity

Kalshi is committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. If you are passionate about what you do and want to use your talents to support our mission and values, we’d love to hear from you.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Buying software and services is still slow and fragmented at most companies. Employees don't know how to request what they need, approvals stall across finance, legal, and security, purchase orders live in a separate system from the bills that pay them, and finance teams spend month-end matching it all together by hand.

Ramp's Procurement team builds the system that connects every step of that process, from the first purchase request through sourcing, approvals, purchase orders, receiving, and matching bills and contracts back to what was ordered. Procurement sits upstream of payments and works closely with Bill Pay, Accounting, and ERP integrations, so the systems we build shape how money leaves a business long before a payment goes out.


We're looking for a senior backend engineer to own a core part of that system. You'll take responsibility for a product area such as the purchase order lifecycle, PO and bill matching, PO coding and accruals, or supplier and ERP integrations, set its technical direction within the team, and keep it healthy as customers and complexity grow.   • Design data models that keep purchase orders, receipts, bills, and accounting data accurate and traceable from request to payment

  • Build and improve integrations with ERPs and supplier systems that stay consistent through retries, partial failures, and edits on either side

  • Help build AI-assisted features, such as automated PO coding and intelligent matching, that reduce manual work for finance and procurement teams

  • Drive technical direction for your area, connecting long-term system health to the team's roadmap

  • Work cross-functionally with product, design, and data, and with partner teams across Bill Pay, Accounting, to ship features across the full procurement lifecycle

  • Raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship


What You'll Need

  • A track record of owning a system or product area end to end: spotting problems before they are assigned, proposing the fix & working with relevant stakeholders, and shaping the area's technical direction over time

  • Product sense: you care about the customer problem, can work through ambiguous enterprise requirements, and push back when the spec is wrong

Hut 8 brings exceptional people together to solve the world’s most consequential problems at the intersection of energy and technology. Today, that means building infrastructure for AI at a pace and scale without precedent. Tomorrow, it could mean powering a new era of innovation through robotics, advanced manufacturing, or an industry that does not yet exist. Whatever the technology demands, our ambition holds: to build the defining physical infrastructure company of our generation.

We look for thinkers and builders with the rigor, humility, and ownership to solve problems at this scale. They start from zero and choose truth over tradition. They back the best idea, whatever its source. They bet on themselves and embrace the hard truths that force them to grow. Our commitment is to keep the path from idea to execution short, trust them with critical decisions and the work that follows, and surround them with colleagues whose curiosity extends beyond their expertise.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Mechanical Systems Expert is Managed Services' expert embedded in a data center build - supporting design review and commissioning to ensure cooling systems are operable and maintainable at turnover. Every design decision eventually becomes someone's 3 a.m. problem; this role reviews the design and witnesses the testing on behalf of that person.


Some of the key responsibilities you should expect are the following:

Operability Design Review

Review mechanical and cooling designs - chilled water plants, air and liquid cooling systems, CDUs, CRAHs, heat rejection, water treatment - through an operations lens: maintenance access and laydown, isolation and redundancy behavior, degraded-mode operation, instrumentation adequacy, and failure-mode consequences. File review comments that change designs, not just document concerns.

Construction-Phase Verification

Walk mechanical installations at key milestones: pipe routing and support, valve access, equipment clearances, insulation quality, and cleanliness/flushing protocol compliance - catching operability problems while they're still cheap to fix.

Commissioning Witness

Witness Level 3-5 commissioning of mechanical systems: functional performance tests, staging and failover sequences, failure scenarios, and integrated systems testing. Drive operational issues into the Cx log with clear acceptance criteria and verify closure personally.

Turnover Readiness

Verify mechanical turnover packages: O&Ms, as-builts, valve tags and system labeling, water treatment baselines, spare parts and consumables lists, and PM program inputs (frequencies, procedures, vendor contacts). Validate training actually equips operators to run the plant.

Operations Transition Support

Support early operations stabilization post-turnover: alarm tuning input, setpoint refinement, and first-months troubleshooting alongside the operations team.

Program Feedback

Feed operational lessons into Hut 8 mechanical design standards and the next project's basis of design.

ABOUT YOU

What we're looking for:

  • 8+ years in critical facilities mechanical operations, commissioning, or chief-engineer-track roles.
  • Deep hands-on knowledge of chilled water plants, hydronic systems, and data center cooling topologies - air-cooled, water-cooled, and liquid/direct-to-chip.
  • Level 1-5 commissioning fluency from the witness/operations side, including integrated systems testing.
  • Sharp eye for maintainability in design reviews: access, isolation, and instrumentation gaps.
  • Turnover documentation rigor - you read the O&M before signing for it.
  • Comfortable embedded with a construction team while holding the operations line.
  • Water treatment and cleanliness protocol experience for critical hydronic systems.
  • CFC/EPA certifications, trade licensure, or engineering degree all welcome paths.

ABOUT THE WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Full time on-site in Nueces County, TX.

About us

BVNK is the stablecoin-powered financial stack for enterprises. We're now part of Mastercard, and together we're building a network for every form of money – one that delivers more reach, more capability and more choice.

We enable businesses to build financial products, unlock new markets, and move money in seconds across 130+ countries, with 40+ licenses for fiat and digital assets globally. Processing billions annually, we empower enterprises worldwide to send, receive, convert, and settle stablecoins and fiat seamlessly through a single integration.

Our mission is to accelerate global money movement, and we're assembling a world-class team to make it happen.

Trusted by industry leaders like Corpay, Worldpay, Deel, and Flywire, we deliver the infrastructure that makes new forms of money usable within the financial systems customers already rely on today.

By combining Mastercard's global payment reach and trusted networks with BVNK's stablecoin infrastructure, we're building the trusted operating layer for the evolution of money movement, helping customers participate in emerging digital networks without having to rebuild their businesses around every new innovation.

We're a diverse team spread across EMEA, North America, and APAC, with a shared belief that stablecoins are the new infrastructure layer for financial services, and that BVNK is at the forefront of this shift.

We're incredibly honored to have been recognized by:

  • CNBC World's Top Fintech Companies (2026)
  • FXC Intelligence Top 100 Cross-border Payment Companies (2026)
  • Newsweek's The Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces (three years running, most recently 2025)
  • LinkedIn as one of the Top 20 Startups in the UK (2025)

Location: We offer a Hybrid/Remote working policy. 

FUNCTION: Engineering

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer (Backend) to join our Crypto Payments Orchestration team.

Crypto Payments Orchestration is at the heart of BVNK. The team owns the layer that makes crypto and stablecoin payments behave like simple, programmable money movement. Interviewing with TRM

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

At Augustus, we collapse the stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.

As CDD Analyst at Augustus, you own customer due diligence end to end, from onboarding through periodic and event-driven reviews. You run CIP/CDD on individuals and legal entities, assign customer risk ratings, and run EDD on high-risk customers, complex ownership structures and FBO relationships. We’re building an AI native bank, which is designed to run mostly autonomously. Legacy banks scale KYC with people. We scale it with agents, supporting human decisions. You improve the prompts of our review agents, and you work with Engineering and Product to automate onboarding within our regulatory bouunds. Your judgment sets the standard the agents follow. The goal is to make routine cases disappear so your time goes to the ones that matter.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.
Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

About the Opportunity

OKX is hiring a Head of Tax Information Reporting to build and run our global tax information reporting function. The function covers the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), the EU's DAC8 directive, the amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS 2.0), FATCA, and US Form 1099-DA across multiple reporting entities and a large global user base, with annual reporting across the EU, Brazil, and other CARF jurisdictions.
Most of the work is data: getting the right user, transaction, and balance data out of our platform, reconciling it, and turning it into accurate filings. You will own the relationship with our reporting vendor, the data specification that feeds it, and the quality checks that decide whether a file goes out.
You will run a central function that owns policy, data, vendor, QA, and submission for every entity in scope. Each reporting entity names an accountable signatory. Local compliance and entity leads are consulted on local requirements and support registration where the law requires a local filer. You will work closely with Product, Data Engineering, Finance Operations, Group Tax, Legal, Data Privacy, and the local entity leads.
Location: remote available, with a strong preference for the US or EU. Some travel to OKX offices.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own the end-to-end CARF, DAC8, CRS 2.0, FATCA, and 1099-DA reporting cycle for every OKX entity in scope: population definition, self-certification coverage, data extraction and reconciliation, file production, QA, filing, corrections, and tax authority queries.
  • Define and own the data specification that feeds the tax platform vendor: which users, which transactions, which balances, how they are aggregated by user and jurisdiction, and how they reconcile to the ledger. Work with Product and Data Engineering to build and test the pipeline.
  • Build and run the QA framework. Reconcile every file to source, validate it against the OECD XML schema and local variants, sample-test self-certification reasonableness checks, and run cross-entity consistency checks for users who hold accounts with more than one OKX entity. Nothing files without your release.
  • Manage the tax platform vendor: contract scope, delivery calendar, test cycles, output validation, issue resolution, and the annual renewal decision.
  • Set the group reporting policy and interpret the regimes for OKX: reportable crypto-assets, transfers to unhosted wallets, staking and reward income, retail payment thresholds, residency tie-breakers, and TIN rules, exercising independent technical judgment, supported by Legal and external tax advisers.
  • Own the global tax self-certification design in onboarding, including validation rules, refresh triggers, and the backlog remediation program for existing users, working with Compliance and Product.
  • Define the process for restricting undocumented accounts under DAC8 and CARF, including reason codes and customer communications, with restrictions applied automatically in Product and monitored by the central team.
  • Maintain the entity-by-entity readiness tracker covering domestic enactment, registration, self-certification coverage, and deadlines. Report weekly to the CCO and monthly to the CARF steering committee.
  • Hands-on leader. Build a small, senior team, scaled through the reporting vendor and outside advisers. Coordinate with and train local compliance and entity leads.
  • Support independent testing by Compliance Monitoring, Risk, and Internal Audit, and support tax authority examinations with complete, reproducible records.


What We Look For In You

  • 7+ years in tax information reporting, tax operations, or regulatory data reporting at a global exchange, broker, bank, fintech, or digital asset platform, including at least 3 years leading a team.
  • Hands-on experience in a global, distributed digital asset business: you have worked with exchange or wallet transaction data, multiple legal entities, and users spread across many jurisdictions. This is required.
  • Strong data skills. You can write SQL, define data specifications for engineers, reconcile large transaction datasets to a ledger, and find the gap when the numbers do not tie. You have built or run data quality controls on reporting output.
  • Working knowledge of CARF, DAC8, CRS, and FATCA, including due diligence rules, self-certification requirements, reportable transaction categories, and the XML schemas used for exchange. Direct CARF or DAC8 implementation experience is strongly preferred given live DAC8 obligations and upcoming CARF reporting.
  • Experience managing a tax reporting vendor or reporting platform, including scoping, testing, and holding the vendor to a delivery calendar. the tax platform vendor experience is a plus.
  • Experience building a function from a small base: writing the policy, designing the controls, hiring the team, and running the first cycle.
  • Ability to explain data and tax issues plainly to executives, engineers, and local compliance officers, and to run a steering committee.
  • Judgment on when to escalate, comfort working across US, EU, and Asia time zones, and a record of meeting hard filing deadlines.


Nice to Haves

  • Experience with US Form 1099-DA or 1099-B production, backup withholding, or Qualified Intermediary reporting.
  • Experience with the DAC8 60-day account restriction process or equivalent undocumented account remediation at scale.
  • Familiarity with GDPR requirements for sharing customer data with tax authorities, including data protection impact assessments.
  • Python or similar scripting for data validation, and experience with data warehouse tools such as Databricks.
  • Experience working inside a Three Lines Model, including supporting second-line monitoring and Internal Audit.

Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.


The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But international fintechs and banks are left with two unsatisfying options to choose from: Either build on legacy correspondent banks that are slow and unreliable, or interface with middleware providers that neither move nor hold the dollars directly, but instead rely on underlying legacy banks themselves. At Augustus, we collapse the stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.


We are a group of ex-founders, founding employees of unicorns, and people who dropped out of university because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and Etched.


We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.

The Role

As Commercial & Product Counsel at Augustus, you own the legal work behind everything we build, sell and market in the US. You’re the lawyer the business calls first.

You join new products from day one: you structure them, spot risk early and get them to market without legal becoming the bottleneck. You lead commercial negotiations with our enterprise clients and own contracting end to end, from templates and playbooks to signature. You review and shape our marketing so it ships fast and stays compliant.

You report to Ro, our Global Chief Legal and Risk Officer, and work closely with Product, Sales, Marketing and Compliance. The team is small, so you have full ownership and make the calls yourself.

What you'll do

  • Advise on new products from scoping to launch: structure, terms, disclosures and risk.

  • Lead negotiations with enterprise clients, partners and vendors.

  • Own contracting end to end: templates, playbooks, fallback positions and approval rules.

  • Review marketing, website and sales materials so they ship fast and stay compliant.

  • Work with Compliance on how regulatory requirements translate into product and contract terms.

  • Build the systems once, so Sales can close standard deals without waiting on legal.

Who Will Thrive At Augustus

We believe that throwing smart people with high agency at big problems produces the best outcomes. We’re building a modern correspondent bank, and we win by having a better team. The people who succeed here share the following traits:

  • American Dream: You’d rather shoot for gold than settle for mediocrity. You pick the harder goal and stay optimistic when the odds are against you. If it feels easy, we aimed too low.

  • Live Player: You don’t need permission. You rebuild what’s broken without being asked, challenge how things are done, and move before the perfect moment.

  • Ever to Excel: You can’t accept good enough and you take your work personally. When it matters, you do what it takes and keep raising the bar for yourself and your team.

  • Genuine: You play for the company, not your title or turf. Low ego, low drama, no politics. You say it straight, also upwards and always assume good intent.

This Role Is For You If:

  • When a deal is stuck on legal, you find the structure that gets it done.

  • You’d rather build the system once than review every contract.

  • You make the call yourself, with no partner to check with.

  • You use AI to do work that used to take a team of associates.

  • You want to see how a bank is built from the inside.

This Is Not For You If:

  • You measure your value by risks flagged, not deals closed.

  • You need associates or a precedent bank before you can start.

  • You want a narrow practice area. This role covers whatever the business needs next.

  • You hand disputes to outside counsel and stop thinking about them.

Hard Requirements

Must haves:

  • J.D. and admission to a US state bar (New York preferred).

  • 3+ years of legal experience, split between a leading law firm (technology transactions, commercial or financial services) and at least 1 years in-house at a startup.

  • Track record of negotiating complex commercial agreements and advising product teams directly.

  • Based in New York or willing to relocate.

Strong preference:

  • In-house experience at a fintech or financial institution.

  • Exposure to payments, banking or financial services regulation.

Pay transparency

Compensation packages at Augustus include base salary, equity and benefits. New hire offers are based on a candidate’s experience, expertise and geographic location. The annual US base salary range for this role is 180,000-250,000.

What We Offer

  • Career Growth: You will be given more responsibility and pushed to grow faster than ever before.

  • Network: Your peers are brilliant, highly motivated people. These people will be foundational in your future opportunities.

  • Real Participation: Employees are shareholders. You will think and act like an owner.

  • Perks & Benefits: Relocation support, visa support, the latest Apple gear (MacBook + AirPods), lunch benefit, gym benefit, a beautiful office in the heart of the city, 4x on-/offsites per year, and an annual development budget.

Additional to the global benefits above, we offer localized benefits such as comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance and a 401(k) retirement plan for our US team.

Augustus is committed to creating an inclusive environment where people from all backgrounds can thrive and where different viewpoints and experiences are valued and respected. Augustus will consider all applications for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, religious beliefs, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, neurodiversity, disability, age, parental or veteran status.
